### 📓 Docs Drift Check
⚠️ **15** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/cli/README.md`, `packages/connectors/connector-imap/README.md`, `packages/core/README.md`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files. Nothing else in this diff resolved to a documentable surface (no symbol, route or SDK anchor derived from **15** changed package(s)).

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **15** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/cli/README.md`, `packages/connectors/connector-imap/README.md`, `packages/core/README.md`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **163** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 61c079862ac726a1e16fcd73a04122567f475c4a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

## 席位核对 · ACCEPT · devx seat 2 · 2026-10-27T01:08Z

Seat `domain:devx#2` (#20163) · `session_01Q4MDXRbEJCNdPAP4SiXwp9` · reviewed head `894bdb38` · card #26208, claim 6430866829 (wave 8, delta F). PR carries `Fixes #26208`.

- **Scope:** 17 files, +60/−0: one `### Module resolution` paragraph in `content/docs/plugins/development.mdx`, one identical line in 15 package READMEs, one root `.changeset/` file (patch × 15). Not governed (`check-governed-merges`: tier null). No `exports` change, no `typesVersions`, no `ui/`.
- **Premise:** I spot-checked the package manifests on the PR head: `spec` (`./data`, `./system`, `./kernel`…), `cli` (`./console`, `./hook-body`), `types` (`./node`), `core` (`./logger`) and `create-objectstack` (`./created-summary`) all declare subpaths only through `exports`, with no `typesVersions`, so node10 cannot see them. The thread's count (exactly these 15 among non-private packages) stands.
- **Placement:** the paragraph sits under the guide's `tsconfig.json` step, whose example already uses `"moduleResolution": "bundler"`, so "(as above)" is true. Each README line links that anchor; `published-readme-links` and `doc-anchors` passed in the thread's run.
- **Accuracy:** "`node10` is the default when `module` is `commonjs`" holds for the TypeScript 5.x line this repo uses. Nit, not blocking: the changeset's "while the root entry still appears to work" does not apply to `create-objectstack`, which has no root entry (only `./created-summary`); true for the other 14.
- **Changeset:** patch is right, since the README ships in each tarball; the `Clause-②` / `Metadata-protocol` lines follow the root `.changeset/` convention.

Landing: when CI is green on this head, the seat readies the PR and arms auto-merge.
